title: India news: Protests against election chief escalate as Gandhi, Cockroach party allege 'rigged' vote
summary: Police have used tear gas on protests by the opposition Congress party demanding India's election commission head steps down, following a report alleging "rigged" elections. DW has more.

image.caption: The cockroach movement said it would launch protests across India on October 2 if ​the eelction chief does not resign by SaturdayImage: Abiraj Kumar Arulgnanakumar/DW

blocks.text: Election chief under pressure as protests escalate

Protesters from various groups gathered in Delhi on Friday demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, amid a growing controversy over reported differences within the Election Commission of India (ECI).

on September 23, which reported that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had formally raised objections at least 14 times over a 10-month period to decisions concerning electoral rolls and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) process. The report said some of the decisions had been taken without their knowledge.

the suggestion of an internal breakdown, saying that differences expressed through internal notes are part of the normal decision-making process and that the final decisions of the three-member Commission were unanimous.
On Thursday, the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) gave Gyanesh Kumar
and warned that it would launch a nationwide agitation, including a second protest at Jantar Mantar, if he did not step down.

On Friday, CPI(ML) Liberation leader Dipankar Bhattacharya, AISA leader Neha Bora — who had gone on hunger strike during the first Jantar Mantar protest — senior advocate Prashant Bhushan and activist Yogendra Yadav joined the demonstration.

The Delhi Police had heavily barricaded the area around Jantar Mantar and did not allow protesters to enter the designated protest site. Several activists were detained within minutes of arriving at the spot.

Speaking to DW, Neha Bora accused the Election Commission of “stealing votes” and acting against democracy. She demanded Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation and said the protesters would continue their movement.
Dipankar Bhattacharya told DW that the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) should be scrapped and that fresh elections should be held in several states.
